column2: Act Nine
The Fall of Midgard
Roller Coaster Falling Down

Above their heads, iron-black rails rose steeply into the air, as high as a fifty-story building, twisting like the body of an enormous snake before plunging back down. A train of roller-coaster cars climbed to the summit amid its passengers' screams, slowing almost to a stop. Ahead lay a sheer drop like the edge of a cliff. The riders held their breath, too frightened to scream as the precipice crept nearer, like people on the guillotine waiting for the blade to fall.
“That's the Midgard Serpent, the world's most thrilling high-speed roller coaster. One hundred fifty meters high, with a top speed of two hundred fifty kilometers an hour,” Anjou said.

Chu Zihang gazed out over the sunlit amusement park: Six Flags. In a park devoted to thrills and excitement, roller coasters were everywhere. Train after steel train raced across tracks that crisscrossed the sky, while screams rose and fell. He, meanwhile, sat on what was probably the least thrilling attraction in the place: the Ferris wheel. The leisurely contraption had taken fifteen minutes to lift their two-person gondola to the top. From here the mountains curved as gracefully as a young woman's figure, a pleasure to look at.
“Now it's time for your entrance orientation.” Chu Zihang looked away from the view, his expression solemn.

“But, senior... we're on a Ferris wheel!” Xia Mi's eyes widened in surprise, like an Ultraman on patrol suddenly encountering a little monster. A slender, soft lock of hair bobbed before her bright eyes.

“Yes. I chose the Ferris wheel deliberately. Our entrance orientation has to take place away from crowds. This gondola seats two, we're fifty meters above the ground, and we'll remain here for ten minutes. That's enough time for me to finish.”
Xia Mi covered her face. “And here I thought my beauty had finally opened your eyes... Hey! Do you know what taking a girl on a Ferris wheel means?”
Chu Zihang's cold face twitched slightly. It was not inner turmoil but alarm: he realized there might indeed be gaps in his knowledge.
“Is a Ferris wheel... different from the other rides?” he asked cautiously.
“Do you know the three sacred places for a date?” Xia Mi sighed.
Chu Zihang shook his head. He had studied books on female psychology and knew something about women's hormone secretion during romance. But the “three sacred places”...
“The movies, the aquarium, and the Ferris wheel.” Xia Mi counted them off on her fingers.

Chu Zihang's expression grew even worse as memories came back to him. In high school, to thank the cheerleading captain for cheering them on at a basketball game against another school, he had taken her to a movie. Naturally, once he had repaid the favor, he had not contacted her again. Afterward, the girl who always wore a short skirt and a high ponytail seemed to look at him with reproach in her eyes, though he could not quite understand why. He had also taken the head of Shilan High's dance troupe to an aquarium and explained how male seahorses raise their young in brood pouches. She had giggled the whole way, looking almost delirious. Chu Zihang had taken her because they were working together on an extracurricular paper about marine animals. Once it was finished, he had not contacted her again...

“A movie theater is dark, so a girl naturally feels she can depend on the boy. And during a horror movie he has the perfect excuse to hold her hand! Taking her to an aquarium makes you look refined and fond of animals. Girls like caring boys, and in a blue underwater tunnel, there's a mysterious feeling that the two of you are alone together in another world. A Ferris wheel is the best place to confess your feelings. Nobody can interrupt you, and the girl can't run away. When you reach the top, pull out the rose you've prepared, get down on one knee, and confess! You have a whole ten minutes. For a boy who knows how to talk, ten minutes is enough to move a sea turtle to tears!” Teacher Xia Mi instructed him earnestly.
“Why would you want to move a sea turtle?” A little sweat appeared at Chu Zihang's temple.
“That's not the point!” Xia Mi looked embarrassed. “The point is, a Ferris wheel is romantic! You can't bring up unpleasant subjects in a romantic place.”
“Does... entrance orientation count as an unpleasant subject?”
“Depends what you compare it with.” Xia Mi shrugged.
Chu Zihang relaxed slightly. Apparently, it was not the most unpleasant subject, at least.
“Compared with taking out a dead spider, throwing it at a girl, and laughing your head off, entrance orientation isn't all that unpleasant,” Xia Mi went on.
Chu Zihang looked as though he had just eaten the dead spider.

“Come to think of it, this is my first time coming to an amusement park with someone!” Xia Mi looked into the distance. Amid the screams, the dragonlike coaster thundered upward in a spiral, as if trying to escape gravity.

Chu Zihang was surprised. He was a regular at amusement parks. In “Dad's” view, nothing showed family affection better than a park festooned with colorful flags. Television commercials always showed some goofy kid wearing a clown's red nose, with a “successful, loving dad” on one side and a “gentle, virtuous mom” on the other. The three would grin foolishly at the camera, and click, a photograph would capture them against a backdrop of bright rides. “Dad” loved that feeling, just as he liked printing photographs of himself with his bosses and hanging them on the wall. So Chu Zihang had been made to pose for countless close-ups at amusement parks.
The other man's way of spending time with his son was to take him to a public bathhouse, drink Coke while soaking in cloudy water, and ask Chu Zihang to scrub his back.

“I've always wanted to come to an amusement park. I used to sneak here by myself, but it wasn't any fun.” Xia Mi gripped the rail by the window, its shadow falling across her soft face. Her eyes were deep, hidden in the shade.
“Really?” Xia Mi did not strike Chu Zihang as a girl from a poor family, and a trip to an amusement park did not cost much.

“I have an older brother. He has an intellectual disability.” Xia Mi pouted like a child. “He can't come to an amusement park. He can't go on any rides, and the staff would chase him away. Every weekend Mom and Dad stayed home with him. If I wanted to go, I had to go alone, and who wants to walk around an amusement park by herself?”
“I thought you were spoiled at home,” Chu Zihang said casually.
“Why?” Xia Mi asked.

Chu Zihang did not know how to answer. There was no particular reason. She simply seemed like the little-princess type, a little like Liu Miaomiao. What parents would not dote on a daughter like that? She seemed born for parents to show off proudly to everyone else. Her smile looked as though it could radiate sunshine.

“We're twins. My brother was born six hours before me. I wouldn't come out, and the doctors and nurses were so worried about me that they forgot to look after him. He couldn't breathe and was deprived of oxygen for half an hour, so he ended up disabled,” Xia Mi said. “Mom and Dad said he gave his chance to me. He could have been smart and outstanding too. So I was supposed to do better than everyone else, because half of my share belonged to him... No matter how hard I worked, nobody praised me...” Xia Mi stuck out her tongue. “Oh, a young master like you wouldn't understand. Did your mom and dad come to your parent-teacher meetings?”

Chu Zihang nodded. “Dad” regarded parent-teacher meetings as important occasions to display family harmony. He and Mom always arrived looking splendid, treating the teachers as solemnly as they would investors.

“But mine hardly ever came. I'd been top of my class since I was little, so they weren't impressed anymore. In my first year of high school, I won a gold medal in the Math Olympiad. I ran home excited to tell them, but the house was a mess. Furniture had been knocked over, clothes and quilts were everywhere, and every few steps I treaded on torn cloth and stuffing. Nobody was home. I couldn't reach them on their phones, so I sat in the middle of the mess and waited until I fell asleep. Mom and Dad didn't get back until morning. They said my brother had gotten upset somehow, banging his head against the wall and tearing things apart. They got a lot of people to help take him to the hospital, where he was given a sedative, and stayed with him all night.” Xia Mi hugged her knees, lost in thought. “They were exhausted. They told me what had happened to him and went to bed. Nobody asked how I'd spent the night, and nobody cared that I'd won.”
“You... don't like your brother?” Chu Zihang asked.

“No, I love him. Maybe because we spent ten months together in Mom's belly, he's very attached to me. When he can't calm down and Mom and Dad don't know what to do, all I have to do is talk to him and he settles down. That time he lost his temper because I was staying at school for extra lessons before the Olympiad, and he never saw me. He thought Mom and Dad had hidden me, so he got angry. It wasn't really an episode. Later, when I went to see him at the hospital, he was lying in bed staring hard at the ceiling, refusing to sleep. But the moment he saw me, his eyes changed. I gave him my hand to hold, and he sniffed it. Once he was sure I smelled and looked right, that I really was his little sister, he held my hand and fell asleep.” Xia Mi smiled. “He's just like a puppy. Could you ever dislike your own puppy?”
“I can't have a dog. Mom is allergic to cat and dog hair.” Chu Zihang apologetically explained that he had never had the chance to become attached to an animal.

“I hate it when people bully him. When we were little, I took him out shopping. Everyone looked at him with disgust, asking what sort of irresponsible parents would let a little girl take an idiot out by herself. He may be slow, but he's very sensitive. He clutched my skirt and glared fiercely at them. Their stares made me uncomfortable, and suddenly I felt ashamed of him too. On the way home I wouldn't let him come near me. I told him to follow ten meters behind, and if he came closer, I wouldn't speak to him. He was afraid of that, so he followed me, keeping exactly ten meters away. I was upset and walked fast without looking back. After a while I turned around and couldn't find him. I was so frightened I ran back. I found him in an alley, pinned to the ground by a group of people who were beating him. Their leader was a boy from my school who I knew wanted to date me. When he saw me, he hurried to say he'd been passing by and noticed an idiot sneaking along behind me, staring at my legs with a nasty grin. So he'd called a few friends to pin him down, but the idiot was very strong and they'd had a hard time of it. They hadn't even had time to say hello to me.” Xia Mi sighed. “I saw my brother in the middle of the crowd, his face covered in blood and dirt. When he saw me, he started grinning, even with a foot on his face. I felt so awful... I told him I wasn't angry with him, and he could hit them back.”
“What did you mean?”

“He's very strong. All those people together couldn't beat him. But I'd forbidden him to hit people whenever he liked. If he hit someone, I wouldn't speak to him for a month...” Xia Mi said. “So he knocked all the boys flat, and I let him hold the hem of my skirt again and took him home. Those idiots never understood why he kept looking at my legs. He was really looking at my skirt, because he always followed me holding the hem.”
“You're very good to your brother.”
“But sometimes I wish he'd never been born,” Xia Mi said softly. “Then he wouldn't have had to suffer so much.”
“If he could come to an amusement park, I bet he'd be happy.” Xia Mi fell into thought again.
Chu Zihang sat there blankly, unsure what to say. He did not know why Xia Mi had told him about her family, and in truth he did not particularly want to know.

Everyone had things they kept hidden in their hearts, didn't they? Like the “absolute territory” in EVA, an absolute domain of the soul where no one else was welcome. In his heart, for example, was a Maybach riddled with holes. When he woke suddenly from a dream, he often felt he was still sitting in that car, with rain pouring outside and that song playing over and over on the stereo. He never told anyone about it, because no one would understand. And if that was so, why tell them?

Some memories were unpleasant. You could bear the bitterness yourself; there was nothing worth sharing. Would anyone willingly sit with you in a broken car on a cold, bleak night and listen to the rain?
Really, Xia Mi need not have told him any of this either.

Of course, Chu Zihang had been moved a little. And, as Lu Mingfei said, sometimes he was a busybody who could not leave other people's affairs alone. If he had been in that alley years ago, he probably would not have stood by. Before the boys dragged Xia Mi's brother into the alley, he would have stepped in front of him, his face cold. If the boys wanted a fight, wonderful: Chu Zihang was a born killer. Then the thing that made Xia Mi unhappy would never have happened, and her brother could have followed her all the way home. Along the long lane, a girl in a white sundress edged with lace would walk, with her brother following behind, grinning foolishly.
But he had not been there. He had never shared his time with anyone, not even Susie. He had only sat alone in the Maybach on a rainy night, listening to an Irish folk song.

He felt he ought to break the awkward silence. He cleared his throat. “This is another form of blood sorrow. For people like us, coming together often stems from recognizing a shared bloodline and the loneliness of being unable to fit into society...”

“There you go again! We're still on the Ferris wheel! The weather's lovely and the view is great. Can't we talk about life and our dreams? I learned all that orientation stuff in prep school.” Xia Mi glared at him.

“Dear passengers, you've talked quite enough about life and dreams. Your ten minutes are up. Welcome back to the ground.” The gondola door suddenly opened, and a silver-haired old fellow outside bowed slightly like an attendant.
“P-Principal?” Chu Zihang and Xia Mi were both stunned.
Time seemed to have passed much faster than usual. The gondola had somehow returned to the ground, where Principal Anjou stood with Lu Mingfei, whose face was full of envy, jealousy, and resentment.

“I'm attending an event with Mingfei, and we had the afternoon free. Mingfei said he'd never been to Six Flags, and complained that we'd sent him to an event instead of letting him orient a pretty junior, so I brought him to have a look.” Anjou patted Xia Mi's soft hand where it rested on his arm.
“I thought the principal would be some stuffy old man, but you actually eat mint ice cream? Mint is really trendy! They just introduced it.” Xia Mi skipped along with her arm through Anjou's.

“Actually, I prefer lemon. But when you get old, you often regret how few new things remain in the life you have left, so you have to try whatever's newest.” Anjou smiled happily. “Ah, walking with a pretty girl makes me feel much younger. I can feel passion flowing through my veins!”
“Cut the crap! That's the old man's long-dormant testosterone flowing, you bastard!” Lu Mingfei grumbled inwardly, following ten meters behind.

Anjou and Xia Mi walked arm in arm ahead, he eating a cup of mint ice-cream beads, she one with strawberry sauce. They looked inexplicably harmonious, like a grandfather and granddaughter. They had completely forgotten the two third wheels behind them, even neglecting to buy ice cream for Lu Mingfei and Chu Zihang.

“Senior! He's stealing what you were supposed to guard!” Lu Mingfei nudged Chu Zihang with his shoulder. “I'm really not trying to stir things up, but if I were you, I couldn't stand that old guy stealing my girl right in front of me!”

He felt a little disappointed himself. Such a stunning junior was rare, and the expressionless senior had won her over with a hundred million dollars' worth of effort. Still, he had to admit that however you looked at it, Chu Zihang and Xia Mi were well matched: their looks, their bearing, and even their scholarly way of speaking.
“What's that got to do with me?” Chu Zihang kept a straight face.
A powerful wind swept past the backs of their heads with a thunderous vibration. The screams that followed nearly pierced their eardrums.

Above their heads, iron-black rails rose steeply into the air, as high as a fifty-story building, twisting like the body of an enormous snake before plunging back down. A train of roller-coaster cars climbed to the summit amid its passengers' screams, slowing almost to a stop. Ahead lay a sheer drop like the edge of a cliff. The riders held their breath, too frightened to scream as the precipice crept nearer, like people on the guillotine waiting for the blade to fall.
“That's the Midgard Serpent, the world's most thrilling high-speed roller coaster. One hundred fifty meters high, with a top speed of two hundred fifty kilometers an hour,” Anjou said.
The coaster entered the downward track, seemingly in free fall. Screams swept across the park again, startling a pigeon flying overhead so badly that its wings jerked and it nearly fell from the sky.
Lu Mingfei shuddered. He saw Xia Mi jump excitedly and point up at the sky.

“She can't be serious, can she? What kind of girl rides a roller coaster? You girls like things like Snow White's castle, right? You're happy just hugging Mickey Mouse for a photograph, right?” Lu Mingfei shouted inwardly, like a man reciting a spell.
“Let's ride that one!” Xia Mi said eagerly.

Lu Mingfei looked to Anjou for help. As an old fellow over 130, surely his heart wasn't up to it... Your life's ambition is to travel the world and kill every Dragon King, right? You don't want to die of a heart attack on a roller coaster before you achieve it, do you? Be brave and tell this crazy girl off! Tell her we should go see Snow White's castle instead!
“Ho! Now that's exciting!” Anjou rubbed his hands. “I can't wait!”
“Have you lost your mind? Aren't you afraid your heart will give out up there?” Lu Mingfei could barely catch his breath.
“Principal, you're amazing!” Xia Mi rested her head on Anjou's shoulder.

Lu Mingfei instinctively wanted to step back, but held himself in check. The roller coaster looked terrifying, but... losing your nerve in front of a pretty junior was a disgrace for life! Suddenly he noticed Chu Zihang had fallen a step behind. He turned and saw his expressionless senior staring at the enormous steel monster, his face twitching slightly.
“Could it be...” Lu Mingfei froze, and for some reason felt a little delighted.
Xia Mi turned around. “First Senior Brother, Second Senior Brother, come on!”
When had their titles changed to First and Second Senior Brother? Was this Journey to the West? Why did he suddenly feel like Zhu Bajie?

Xia Mi and Anjou had already rushed toward the end of the snaking line. Their excitement was apparently too great to contain; they hardly wanted to bother with the other two, and had invited them along only out of courtesy.
“Senior, I saw your face twitch,” Lu Mingfei said under his breath.
“I get a little motion-sick,” Chu Zihang said quietly.

“Come on. If you're scared, you're scared. Nothing to be ashamed of. Even if it is embarrassing, it won't kill you. Senior, just admit your favorite ride is really Snow White's castle, and we'll go there together... If you force yourself, neither of us will come out of it well!” Lu Mingfei coaxed him patiently, his face grave.
“My favorite attraction is actually Winnie the Pooh and His Friends.”
“Hurry up!” Xia Mi waved at them from a distance.
“Yeah! Coming, coming!” Lu Mingfei smiled back instinctively. As soon as he had said it, he wanted to slap himself.
“Don't be silly. Neither Winnie the Pooh nor Snow White can save us now,” Chu Zihang murmured.

Lu Mingfei fastened his safety restraint and glanced at Chu Zihang beside him. Chu Zihang gripped the handles over his shoulders, pale and staring straight ahead, as if a teacher had punished him for misbehaving by making him sit up straight. Anjou and Xia Mi had claimed the front row so they could enjoy the thrill of plunging headfirst toward the ground against the wind. Both had been eager and excited all along.

The launch tunnel was pitch-dark. Two rows of red lights flashed along the track, making the atmosphere inexplicably tenser. An attendant checked everyone's restraints. “Please keep your head firmly against the headrest to avoid straining your neck from the acceleration.”

Damn it, couldn't they just say nothing? To mention neck injuries so casually... It was like an executioner gently telling you to relax your muscles before the blade fell, or your poop might fly out and make an ugly mess. A hundred Shaanxi waist-drum players were pounding away in Lu Mingfei's heart, and he knew there were a hundred in Chu Zihang's too. How he wished he had a Yanling like Star Platinum to cut out the next minute. In the blink of an eye the coaster would be at the end, and he could stand up calmly and say, “That was fun. I'd love to do it again, but the line takes too long. How about we go see Snow White's castle...”
The attendants withdrew into the darkness. An ominous alarm swept through the tunnel, and the red lights suddenly flashed ten times faster. Adrenaline surged.
Suddenly all the red lights went out! The alarm stopped! One suffocating second of dead silence.

Lu Mingfei felt as if he were riding a rocket, and the rocket had ignited! Acceleration pressed him hard into his seat. The wind pressure was so great his eyeballs seemed about to burst, even more extreme than Anjou's Maserati.

Lu Mingfei and Chu Zihang could not help roaring. Everyone was screaming instinctively, unable to stop until every last breath had been forced from their lungs. Amid the screams came the laughter of Anjou and Xia Mi... which only made it more unbearable.

Light rushed at them as the coaster shot out of the launch tunnel at an astonishing 250 kilometers an hour. Ahead, the rising track was nearly vertical, like a ladder into the sky. Lu Mingfei felt certain they would smash into it and be pulverized. But the coaster began climbing and twisting vertically. White clouds in the blue sky spun rapidly across his vision, like a kaleidoscope.

It all felt unreal to Lu Mingfei: the shrieking wind, the spinning clouds, the sky rushing at him. Time seemed to race past him, the years slipping by, black hair turning white in an instant. It made him want to sigh softly.
Someone really did sigh softly.
“Brother, if you want to summon me, you have nine seconds. After that, there won't be anyone in the world who can save you.”

Lu Mingfei froze, then lashed out viciously with his foot at the person beside him—not the deathly pale Chu Zihang, but Lu Mingze. The fellow wore casual clothes and sat with his legs crossed, perfectly at ease, holding a cup of ice-cream beads drizzled with yellow-peach sauce. A plastic spoon in his mouth, he looked up at the sky and sighed.

The idea of any normal person eating ice cream on a roller coaster traveling 250 kilometers an hour and twisting through 360 degrees was nonsense. The enormous centrifugal force would have plastered the ice cream and peach sauce across his face.
But Lu Mingze was clearly not normal. He had stopped the entire roller coaster!

The whole amusement park had suddenly turned gray, like a photograph frozen in an instant. Only Lu Mingfei and Lu Mingze were still in color, and only the people in color could move. Without warning, without the slightest sensation of slowing, their speed had dropped from 250 kilometers an hour to zero. Lu Mingfei looked around trembling. The coaster hung suspended in midair, far from both sky and ground, while the towering track resembled the bones of a giant dragon.
“Don't squirm. You really could fall,” Lu Mingze warned. Yet he had not even fastened his own restraint, and sat there comfortably eating ice cream.
“Damn it! Can you make an appointment next time? Pick a better time? I don't want to entertain some devil salesman on a roller coaster!”
“The accident rate for roller coasters is about one in 250 million,” Lu Mingze said. “Much safer than flying.”
“I know. Can't I just join in and scream with everybody else to make the atmosphere more festive?”
“But it isn't zero,” Lu Mingze said mildly.
Lu Mingfei froze.
“That probability means that for every 250 million roller-coaster rides in the world, there will be one accident. For the people caught in that accident, the death rate is a hundred percent.”
A chill ran through Lu Mingfei. “Don't jinx it!”

Lu Mingze shrugged. “To a statistician, one in 250 million is a probability. But to the passengers on the coaster, everything seems like fate. They watch one group of visitors after another get on, scream, and return safely to the ground, so they believe they'll be fine too. Then they get on, and suddenly the ending changes.” Lu Mingze pointed into the distance. “The last train went to heaven. This one is going to hell!”

Lu Mingfei followed his finger and saw cracks spreading across a section of track in the distance. The track was breaking apart! No, it was worse than that: it was twisting. Imagine someone gripping both ends of a snake's spine and turning them in opposite directions. At this rate the track would become one enormous twisted braid!
Talk about a jinx... No, this was a devil's curse! The train really was going to hell!
“H-help!” Lu Mingfei trembled.

“Sure! One quarter of your life, and I'll take care of it!” By the time he said it, Lu Mingze was no longer sitting beside Lu Mingfei. He had climbed to the front row and was leaning over Xia Mi, carefully smearing yellow-peach sauce on her face, like a painter wholly absorbed in his beloved work.

“Don't expect me to do it free this time. Do you know how much work it took to cultivate you as a client? When you chase girls, I send flowers. When you buy things, I pay. When you take up a sword to slay a dragon, I wait on you hand and foot. The only thing I haven't done is serve your tea.” Lu Mingze smiled at him. His words were cutting, but his smile was still clear and innocent, rippling with warm sunlight.

A little less than half the rail had broken away. The greater part remained standing only because the main steel girder supported it. In the almost motionless flow of time, the severed section was falling slowly toward the ground with an apocalyptic beauty.
Anjou suddenly moved, as though trying to break free of a restraint. A savage expression flickered across Lu Mingze's face and vanished.
“People who interfere with someone else's business are the worst.” His careless expression returned. “Then I'll leave the situation to him for now.”

Lu Mingze vanished in an instant, as neatly as a pencil mark erased with a rubber. A hand seemingly appeared from nowhere and seized Lu Mingfei by the collar. “Xia Mi, Mingfei, Zihang!” Anjou's deep voice rang out.

The coaster continued to rise slowly, and the severed rail continued to fall slowly. Lu Mingze's disappearance had not returned time to normal. Otherwise, no matter how vigorous and brave Anjou was for his age, he would never have dared unfasten his restraint and reach back from the front row to grab them.
“It's Time Zero!” Chu Zihang realized. Anjou's Yanling happened to be the ability to stretch time.
“What's going on?” Xia Mi looked around in bewilderment.

Lu Mingfei's heart tightened. Above Xia Mi's lips, two strokes of yellow-peach sauce formed a little yellow mustache... Lu Mingze had never left traces in reality before, but whether it was the fried dough stick last time or the peach-sauce mustache now, he seemed to have gained the ability to bridge dreams and reality.
Anjou pointed into the distance. Chu Zihang and Xia Mi both changed color.

The sky was a deep blue, with white clouds drifting across it. A white pigeon hovered almost motionless with its wings spread, like a wax figure molded into the air. But a section of track was falling slowly.
“How much time do we have?” Chu Zihang asked.
“Only six seconds left. Within my domain, I can stretch time about fiftyfold, giving us three hundred seconds,” Anjou said.

“The effect of Time Zero has always been secret, but I suspect it doesn't actually slow the flow of time. It changes the way the four of us perceive it,” Chu Zihang said. “We're the ones who have become faster.”
“Correct, but it doesn't work on humans. I can't speed them up as well,” Anjou said.

“We need a rescue plan immediately, or everyone on this train will die.” Anjou glanced at his wristwatch, but its hands seemed held fast by a magnet. “An ordinary timer is useless inside Time Zero's domain. I'd estimate we have 250 seconds left.”
Chu Zihang and Xia Mi both nodded.
“Hey, I mean, isn't that impossible?” Lu Mingfei trembled. “Why don't we climb down now? At least we'd have a chance of surviving!”

After all, everyone here was among the absolute elite of the hybrids. In martial-arts novels, they would be towering figures of the martial world, and their lives were precious. For the great cause of dragon slaying, shouldn't they encourage one another with “Make sure you survive” and “Our lives are vital to the future of the world,” then jump off and escape?
All three looked up at Lu Mingfei at once. “We haven't reached the point where we have to give up,” Chu Zihang said coolly.

Lu Mingfei shrank back, repelled by their simultaneous sense of justice. Silence fell. He looked left and right at three pairs of rapidly moving eyes, knowing that thoughts were flashing through their heads as busily as a pot of boiling porridge. His own mind was blank. A rescue plan? What nonsense. How much did a roller coaster weigh? At least a dozen tons, racing along a vertical track at 250 kilometers an hour, and only half the track was left. The only possibility was for a Super Stallion heavy-lift helicopter to happen by and hoist the whole train up. But under the blue sky and white clouds, the only thing that could fly was the waxlike bird. Among the four of them, Anjou's and Chu Zihang's Yanling had already been revealed, so all he could hope was that Xia Mi's ability was “Yanling: Transform into a Super Stallion”...
The coaster rose another few dozen meters. Slowed fiftyfold by the Yanling, it crawled like a snail climbing a grape arbor.
Chu Zihang suddenly looked up. “This coaster has fin-shaped magnetic brakes!”
Xia Mi blinked. “You mean we can brake?”
“Hey, if we brake now, won't we just stop in midair?” Lu Mingfei asked.

“We won't remain suspended.” Chu Zihang said, “Fin-shaped magnetic brakes are special equipment on strata coasters. Only three roller coasters in the world have this system. The train itself has no engine. After electromagnetic acceleration gives it its initial speed, it climbs the track, converting kinetic energy into potential energy, and gradually slows.”
Anjou's eyes lit up. “When it reaches the top, its speed is close to zero!”

Chu Zihang nodded. “The Midgard Serpent's track is like an arched bridge. The train has just enough kinetic energy to pass the highest point. Then it enters the descent, potential energy turns back into kinetic energy, and it speeds up again. Finally it enters the electromagnetic braking tunnel and returns to the ground.”

“But we don't have a descending track anymore... After we pass the top... we'll turn into an iron dragon flying through... no, falling straight out of the sky!” Lu Mingfei said. Suddenly high-school physics was back in session.

“But we have fin brakes! They were originally designed as a joke on the passengers. As the train is about to pass the top, it's already moving very slowly. A little braking is enough to leave it without the kinetic energy to get over the crest. It rolls backward down the ascent and returns to the launch tunnel.”
“Hey, how do you know all that? Isn't Winnie the Pooh and His Friends your favorite? You were trembling when you heard we were riding the coaster!” Lu Mingfei said.
“I wasn't confident, so I looked it up on my phone while we were in line...”
“What a tech geek! You've proved yourself again!”

“Yes,” Anjou said. “It's a joke. When riders see the coaster going backward, they usually think something's broken and scream in terror. Before they've finished screaming, the train is safely back in the launch tunnel. Some have felt they came back from the dead, wept, and found religion afterward.”
“The fin brakes are there to make us find religion?” Lu Mingfei's thoughts were a mess. “Religion can only save your soul... Have we already given up on saving our bodies?”
“No,” Xia Mi said. “The fin brakes can send us back to the launch tunnel, so we won't need the descending track.”

Lu Mingfei finally understood, and immediately felt a little inferior. Apparently everyone else had understood the moment Chu Zihang mentioned the fin brakes. The high-school physics lesson had been just for him.
“But the fin brakes can only stop the coaster when its speed is nearly zero,” Anjou said. “We have to trigger them as we approach the highest point.”
“That won't be a problem,” Chu Zihang said. “In Time Zero's domain, time is stretched out. We can control the timing precisely.”
“How do we activate the fin brakes?” Xia Mi asked loudly.

“The train has a transformer at the back. It steps up the low-voltage current from the track to high voltage to drive the fin brakes. But the control switch is undoubtedly in the control room below,” Anjou said. “There isn't time to get down there now.”
“Why do you all seem so familiar with roller coasters?” Lu Mingfei marveled.

“As a roller-coaster enthusiast, I've studied them.” Anjou hesitated. “It isn't very convenient for me to come and ride one by myself, which is why I said I'd bring you to see it today... It's the same reason fathers often eat ice cream under the pretext of keeping their children company.”
“If I open the rear housing, I should be able to pull out the live wire and spark it in midair to activate the fin brakes,” Chu Zihang said. “My specialty is alchemical mechanics.”
“Wow! Science guys are so handsome!” Stars shone in Xia Mi's eyes.
“Then hurry!” Lu Mingfei's eyes widened. “Swoon over him later!”
Chu Zihang drove Anjou's folding knife into the housing and sliced straight through the metal shell. With the transformer exposed, he easily stripped out two wires.
“The red one's live, the blue one's neutral. Touch them together and the fin brakes will start.” He showed Lu Mingfei the wires. “Braking only takes three or four seconds. The key is timing.”
“This half of the track is going to break too, isn't it?” Lu Mingfei looked around.

While they worked, the track around them was coming apart at a visibly increasing rate. It twisted farther and farther, cracks spreading rapidly. Screws that held the rails to the girder burst out one after another. Under Time Zero, they drifted past Lu Mingfei's ears, trailing long, tearing sounds. He thought it looked rather amusing and reached out to touch one, but Chu Zihang shouted at him to stop.
“They look slower to you, but their kinetic energy is still enormous.” Chu Zihang pulled out an expired membership card and held it in front of a screw. The screw pierced it, leaving a jagged hole.
“In normal time, they're as fast as bullets!” Chu Zihang said.
Cold sweat covered Lu Mingfei. He had almost taken a bullet through his finger.
“Hurry! We don't have much time!” Xia Mi called from the front.

Anjou remained upright in the front row, staring ahead, his pupils brilliant gold. The deep-red rose in his suit's buttonhole swayed, broke apart, and scattered in the wind at a speed slowed dozens of times. The old man was not deliberately striking a dramatic pose. Lu Mingfei climbed over and saw that the nosebleed spraying from Anjou's face was as shockingly red as the rose.

He was exerting all his strength to maintain Time Zero's domain. The domain of such a high-order Yanling drained Anjou's mental energy as if drawing water. At first he had only grown mentally tired, but now even his body could no longer bear it.
“Principal, you're gushing blood.” Unable to keep his hands to himself, Lu Mingfei wiped it away.
“You can still be this clueless at a time like this? The principal's about to gush tears too...” Xia Mi looked thoroughly exasperated.
“Take a look behind you. I doubt you'll still be able to joke,” Anjou said quietly.

Lu Mingfei turned and shuddered in silence. So many distorted faces together looked like a work of art depicting despair. The falling section of track was reflected in every pair of eyes. Mouths stretched to their limits emitted heart-rending cries, drawn out by Time Zero into notes as long as a violin's. The passengers had all realized they were racing toward death. Lu Mingfei had never imagined a person's face could twist so horribly with terror. Even the pretty girl he had glanced at a few extra times before boarding now looked like a fanged female ghost.
No... like souls suffering in hell.
Lu Mingfei swallowed, his scalp tingling.

“There's little time. Hurry! We have to activate the fin brakes about ten meters before the coaster reaches the top. Too early, and we'll be moving too fast; the brakes might lock. Too late, and if we pass the top, it's all over,” Anjou said. “I can't help you. I may lose consciousness at any moment. Chu Zihang, this is an operation. You're the commissioner, and you have full command.”
“Understood.” Chu Zihang nodded.
At that moment the falling curved section of track struck the ground and plunged into a circus tent, throwing a curtain of dust into the sky.

“Xia Mi, look after the principal. Make sure his restraint is fastened. If he can't hold on, Time Zero's domain will end. Remember, you're still on a high-speed roller coaster. Lu Mingfei, observe from the front and signal me at ten meters. I'll ignite the circuit at the rear.” With that, Chu Zihang climbed toward the back.

The dust rose swiftly and fragments of track flew, a heart-stopping sight. It looked like a documentary of humanity's final moments, played in slow motion. Lu Mingfei took a deep breath and looked back at Chu Zihang, who hung half out of the rear of the train, live wire in hand, looking toward the front.
Lu Mingfei chuckled. He was laughing at Chu Zihang. The wire in his hand must have carried direct current, charging his whole body until his hair stood on end, as if he had an enormous frizzy perm.
“I really have to hand it to you! You can still laugh now,” Xia Mi said.

“I'm not the only one who laughs when he's nervous. I've always thought that if I were executed as a revolutionary martyr, I'd double over laughing on the ground and say, ‘Ha ha ha ha, don't shoot! Ha ha ha ha, don't shoot! I'll confess, I'll confess, I'll confess everything, ha ha ha!’ The enemy would think I was mocking them and pull the trigger.” Lu Mingfei's voice shook.
“Mingfei, trust your judgment,” Anjou said quietly. The gold in his eyes began to flicker like a dying candle, and even Lu Mingfei could feel the Yanling's domain wavering.
Lu Mingfei raised his hand. This was the signal they had agreed on: when he brought his arm down, the fin brakes would be activated.
The coaster crept forward like a snail.

Suddenly droplets spattered Lu Mingfei's face, and they were enveloped in a fine mist. He wiped his face in surprise. Rain? Surely not; the sky had been clear just moments ago. He looked down and understood. Beside the Midgard Serpent was a large high-pressure fountain that could shoot water 200 meters high. Its pipe ran beneath the circus tent. The rail had pierced the ground and broken the pipe; a high-pressure jet tore through the slowly rising dust and shot higher than the track.
A huge dark shape tumbled through the spray toward the coaster: a broken steel support beam!
“Damn it, don't shoot...” Lu Mingfei murmured.

His mind was still caught on the joke he had just made to Xia Mi. A moment ago he had held a chance of victory; now he was a condemned man about to face a firing squad. No, not a firing squad. With that several-ton beam crashing down on him, his death would be a hundred times uglier than a shooting.
Chu Zihang felt his blood run cold as he watched the deadly blow draw slowly closer. There were always moments that made a person feel small, because there was nothing he could do.

A cry stretched out dozens of times longer slowly tore through the air. He turned and saw a father, face contorted and streaming with tears and snot, lean out and slowly gather his howling son into his arms. He held the boy tight, curving his back like a bow, wrapping his own body around him. The slow motion let Chu Zihang see every detail clearly, including the man's eyes. He had plainly given up hope. In his own passage of time, he had less than a second left before death. At such a height and speed, with steel about to strike, an ordinary person could do nothing. So he did the most meaningless thing: he embraced his son. He wrapped his torso around the boy as the only shield he could provide... though when the impact crushed them, that shield would not last even 0.001 seconds.
“He's your son, isn't he?” Chu Zihang asked softly.
Of course, no one answered him. Chu Zihang stared at the father and son, and the moment stretched on endlessly.
The man stroked his son's hair and actually smiled. What an awful smile it was, full of grief and despair, yet he still smiled for the boy to see. To give him just a little courage.
“Dad, did you smile at me like that too...?” Chu Zihang suddenly leaped up and ran forward over the rows of seats.
“Lu Mingfei! Get to the back and trigger the brakes! I'll block it!” he roared.
“Huh?” Lu Mingfei was stunned.

You'll block it? Come on! Is that something you can block? Do you think you're Voltron, always saying, “I'll form the head”? Stop playing the hero. A hundred of you couldn't stop it! Maybe if you convert to Christianity and believe in God right now, you'll be saved!

Chu Zihang, of course, had no idea how wildly Lu Mingfei's thoughts were racing. They were nearing the highest point now, and the track was leveling out. He charged along the rails like an enraged rhinoceros.

Lu Mingfei scrambled to the rear, grabbed the live wire, and looked back. He drew a sharp breath. Chu Zihang stood at the end of the track, all his skin turned a strange blue-gray. Dense scales pierced through it, growing amid blood and tearing his clothes; his glowing eyes blazed like flames! Sovereign Flame's domain expanded rapidly. Lu Mingfei had never heard of anyone growing scales all over when releasing a Yanling. And the posture of those hands looked like the Buddha's Palm. Facing a beam that huge, shouldn't his senior at least use tai chi to deflect a thousand pounds with four ounces? Why was he using a Shaolin palm technique of utmost hardness and force?
“Trigger it!” Chu Zihang waved.

Lu Mingfei did not move. Chu Zihang's feet stood on the two rails. Activating the fin brakes meant applying high voltage, which would flow away through the rails. The moment he triggered it, the current would pierce Chu Zihang's heart.
“Don't be a fucking idiot! You'll die!” Lu Mingfei shouted back.
“I can only hold it for an instant.” Chu Zihang's voice sank, filled with cold authority. “Trigger it!”
Lu Mingfei gripped the neutral and live wires, both hands shaking.
“Listen. Whether you trigger it or not, I can't get back anymore.” Chu Zihang did not turn around. “Do what you have to. Trust me with the rest.”

That was too brave, wasn't it? What a fine young hero, rushing to the rescue! Lu Mingfei almost wanted to give him a Young Pioneer salute... except he was brave enough to be a fucking idiot! Did he value his own life so little? Lu Mingfei did not salute. Tears welled up instead.
He hooked the neutral and live wires firmly together!

There was no dazzling light in Sovereign Flame's domain. As the temperature rose to its limit, the air currents instead took on a faint black tint. The beam hurtled straight at Chu Zihang; behind him was the coaster. Braking had begun, and high-voltage current made his whole body convulse.
Chu Zihang needed to buy them an instant. He could do it, because he had amplified his blood. Now... he was invincible!

The beam crashed into Sovereign Flame's domain, and the surging power of the Yanling melted it in an instant. Golden molten steel streamed past both sides of Chu Zihang's body. He threw his arms wide, and the superheated air exploded, forcibly scattering the flow of metal!
His vision went blank. He lost his balance and fell into the raging blaze he had ignited.
At last the coaster's speed fell to zero. After an instant's pause, all its steel wheels reversed, carrying it back down the ascent.
At that moment Anjou lost consciousness. The gold faded from his eyes.
Time Zero ended. Lu Mingfei was almost flung away. He had no time to climb back into the train and could only cling to the rail at the rear, dangling outside.

He stared blankly at the figure swallowed by fire... Hey, don't do this. If I'd known, I'd have made a deal with Lu Mingze. At most I'd have lost a quarter of my life, as thanks for helping me save face in front of Chen Wenwen... Just don't die like this... so damn foolishly brave.
A white figure leaped from the roller coaster. It was Xia Mi! She ran along the rails toward the dazzling fire and disappeared into it.
